decisions.decision: Herdr 1 is an allowed runtime alongside Herdr Core. Preserve working native UX instead of requiring a Core-only startup or deleting the Herdr 1 backend. D55 is superseded. decisions.title: Remove the inherited custom updater
decisions.decision: Delete the inherited custom Rust updater and its update/install/restart machinery. Spaceport updates remain a required release capability; this is a replacement transition, not removal of SP-023. Support macOS, Windows, Linux and package-manager installation routes. Sparkle and other platform mechanisms were discussed but no replacement library, Homebrew update-ownership policy, signing identity, release endpoint or publication was approved by this deletion instruction. Preserve release-build refusal while independent identity and update routes remain unverified.

decisions.title: macOS signed preview workflow
decisions.decision: Implement a macOS-only build-and-sign/notarize artifact workflow using 2389 Research signing credentials and bundle ID ai.2389.spaceport. Windows signing is deferred for this work, not removed from the eventual desktop scope. D64 extends this route to tag-triggered GitHub prereleases. App installation, credential upload, automatic updater and general production release enablement remain separate from this decision. Retain the release refusal and distinguish ordinary development builds from signed previews.

Require the exact tagged commit to belong to main and pass full active-platform main CI under D66. Keep signing credentials in a protected signing job; grant release write access only to publication. Doctor Biz's follow-up instruction to push and make it work authorizes main integration, hosted environment setup, credential upload and the first verified tagged preview; keep private signing inputs outside Git.

decisions.title: Sparkle updates for macOS previews
decisions.decision: Use pinned Sparkle 2.10.1 for installed macOS previews, with native Check for Updates UI, consent for automatic checks and automatic installation off by default. Keep development/worktree builds excluded. Embed and sign the framework inside the existing ai.2389.spaceport bundle for Team HD9NM9NSMK. Use a separate Spaceport Ed25519 key outside Git/Cargo and in the protected macos-preview environment; require signed feeds without timed recovery (SUSignedFeedFailureExpirationInterval=0) and pre-extraction archive verification. Publish the signed preview feed as the fixed macos-preview-feed GitHub release asset only after the immutable dated release passes verification. Enforce exact Spaceport app/Team identity in packaging, signing and publication. Sparkle permits trusted publisher key and app identity rotation; do not claim its runtime enforces an unconditional old app ID match. Preserve normal GUI quit/detach and never change Herdr/Core lifecycle. Qualify with isolated real signed update/relaunch fixtures and negative trust/rollback cases. Carry implementation through full source CI and a fresh signed release. Other platform/package routes and overall T12 gates remain open.

decisions.title: Move Spaceport to 2389 Research and pause Windows builds
decisions.decision: Transfer the existing public Spaceport repository from harperreed to 2389-research, retaining its history, releases, PRs and protected signing environment. Update active application, release and signed-feed URLs to 2389-research/spaceport while keeping harperreed as the trusted release actor and preserving bundle identity, signing Team and Sparkle keys. Temporarily skip Spaceport's Windows check, native and packaging CI jobs until Kata h8g5 resolves the native performance failure. The aggregate and macOS preview release gates must require all remaining macOS/Linux jobs and the explicit Windows skipped state. This pause does not pass Windows acceptance, change its performance budget or remove Windows from eventual product scope. Review jvcf under the approved 9s44 fixes narrows the pause to the unchanged Windows performance step. Restore formatting, clippy, unit/CLI, native GUI and input-selected package jobs independently; require their actual results in aggregate and preview source checks. WINDOWS_ENABLED now controls only the performance step, and h8g5 remains a Windows qualification gap. Qualify the repaired main commit and publish a fresh immutable macOS preview version.

decisions.title: Keep Herdr Core behind a disabled-by-default app setting
decisions.decision: Keep Herdr Core available only through explicit opt-in. Add the saved herdr_core_enabled setting, default false for new and existing installs. Show Enable Herdr Core under Settings > General > Experimental with Adds Core terminals and groups. Requires restart. Freeze the effective value for each app session across all windows; saving either value requires restarting Spaceport before runtime behavior changes. While disabled, hide Core UI, prevent Core connections and startup, and refuse Core-only CLI actions explicitly. Preserve saved Core preferences, groups and terminal references, and never stop Core or its terminals. Keep regular Herdr available. This qualifies Core reachability under D58 without removing retained Core support or changing runtime ownership.
decisions.source: Doctor Biz, 2026-11-13: requested a Core feature flag, off by default, because its UI was confusing. Approved the full off behavior, restart requirement, Experimental placement and final design through Q&A, then approved implementation.

decisions.title: Offer a link to install Herdr when Local has no Herdr
decisions.decision: When the Local endpoint cannot start because no herdr executable is found, show a Herdr isn't installed card in place of the reconnecting card, with an Install Herdr button that only opens Herdr's TUI page, https://herdr.dev/tui/ and a Try again button. Retry quietly at the maximum retry delay and clear the card on the next successful connection. Report the state as herdr-missing in spaceport status and host listings. Spaceport never downloads, installs or updates Herdr or runs an installer; the user installs it. Starting an already installed local Herdr when needed stays as D58 allows. This restores the install offer removed for T04 on 2026-11-08, whose reason (a Core-only runtime) D58 and D69 superseded, and is a narrow exception to D58's no-restore clause.
decisions.source: Doctor Biz, 2026-11-16: saw the endless Reconnecting to Local card on a laptop with Herdr removed (Kata 2qr3), approved the fix, then chose to keep the Install Herdr link over a card without one. Then asked that the link go to the TUI page, https://herdr.dev/tui/.

decisions.title: Core route gaps gate Core graduation, not the fork
decisions.decision: The gaps G-CHAT, G-MACHINE, G-PORT and G-FILE describe Herdr Core routes that Herdr does not offer yet. D69 keeps Core behind a disabled-by-default setting, so these gaps no longer gate the Spaceport fork tasks. Remove them from must_close_gaps on T02, T06, T07 and T11. Keep them open in gaps.json and listed in each task's gaps, with their required evidence and forbidden workarounds unchanged. They now gate one later step: enabling Herdr Core by default. Kata rnbn tracks that step. Where Herdr 1 has a route for the same retained behavior, its acceptance scenario must still pass on that route for the fork. A Core leg runs only with Core enabled and is recorded as Core evidence. G-LINK, G-OBS, G-RELEASE and G-PLATFORM are unchanged. This decision invents no Core capability and does not authorize a Spaceport-owned substitute.
decisions.source: Doctor Biz, 2026-11-17: after the registry reconciliation showed four of eight gaps waiting on Herdr changes Spaceport cannot make, approved moving them out of the fork's mandatory scope into a separate Core graduation track.

decisions.title: Terminal links open read-only; the plugin link handler stays removed
decisions.decision: PR #142 removed the client's last live plugin-execution path reachable from an ordinary click: pane.link.activate could answer handled:true, meaning a [[link_handlers]] plugin had already run and claimed the click. Links now open read-only - Spaceport reads the target itself (URL to the browser, file to the default app) and no Herdr plugin handler runs, ever, from a link click. The removal is deliberate fork scope, not an incidental simplification, and matches the upstream no-surprise daemon lifecycle rule. It was never given a decision number; D72 records it.
decisions.source: Crew task apwa, Doctor Biz decision 2026-11-18; PR #142 merged. D-number assigned 2026-11-25 when the register reconciliation (crew task p3es) found the narrowing unrecorded.

decisions.title: Sparkle carries the production update channel
decisions.decision: Use the Sparkle route D65 selected for installed macOS previews as Spaceport's production update mechanism too, and add no other in-app updater. Preview and production are signed builds of one app identity, ai.2389.spaceport, so the compiled build channel - never the bundle ID - decides which feed a copy follows: the macos-preview channel follows the fixed macos-preview-feed appcast, the production channel follows the fixed macos-stable-feed appcast, and development or worktree builds follow none and never check. scripts/release/sparkle.json holds one entry per channel, naming that channel's fixed feed release and its https appcast URL; packaging writes the channel's URL as SUFeedURL and the app refuses to start the updater unless the running bundle carries exactly the address its compiled channel names, requires signed feeds that never expire their rejection, disables automatic installation and authorizes no automatic checks. This decision adds the mechanism only: creating or publishing macos-stable-feed, building or signing a production release, and any tagged production publication need separate owner authorization, the inherited HERDR_RELEASE_VERSION release route stays refused, no workflow builds the production channel, and Windows and Linux update routes remain out of scope under C4.
decisions.source: Doctor Biz, 2026-11-26: chose Sparkle as the production update mechanism, extending the D65 preview route to the production channel, through crew ticket C2 (zafp).

decisions.title: One release naming and download metadata for both signed channels
decisions.decision: The stable channel D73 added publishes the same calendar naming as previews: one immutable YYYYMMDD.COUNTER version behind a vVERSION tag, one version space and one validator for both channels, previews published as GitHub prereleases and stable releases published. scripts/release/channels.json names what each channel publishes - its release title and prerelease flag, the appcast's channel and item titles, and each artifact's file name, signed-artifact kind, display label, platform, architecture, format and minimum system version - while sparkle.json keeps the feed address the app checks; channels.py validates that table, requires its channels to be exactly the app's feed channels, and derives every release, download and page URL from https://github.com/2389-research/spaceport/releases so no address is written twice. A release page carries the signed disk image and SHA256SUMS beside the generated release notes; the fixed feed releases stay prereleases in both channels, so a feed marker never becomes GitHub's latest release or takes a download link from the release it describes; and sparkle-feed.py takes --channel so a stable appcast names the same artifact from the same table. This names and describes the channels only: creating or publishing macos-stable-feed, a production build, sign and packaging route that writes the signed-macos-production artifact kind, and any tagged production publication still need separate owner authorization under G-RELEASE, the inherited HERDR_RELEASE_VERSION route stays refused, signing stays with C1, and Windows and Linux package identities and download metadata stay with C4.
decisions.source: Crew ticket C3 (megk), 2026-11-26: names the stable channel's release, artifact and download metadata on the D73 mechanism; the publication, signing and other-platform authorizations it leaves open stay with their own tickets and the G-RELEASE gate.
